ambiguity_notes: The historical question predates Revision 5. Distinguish automated status determination from automated installation. Applicability, MUSA approval and scheduling adequacy need context.
The catalog describes process isolation. It does not certify a Windows/AWS deployment or prescribe an assessor-approved artifact.
The supplied control text matches the historical Revision 4 style. Baseline selection and tailoring determine applicability and require sources beyond clause text.
Account types include service accounts. Confirm how much of the account-management lifecycle the broad request requires.
The historical quotation uses Revision 4 wording. COTS use alone does not establish that a control is inherited or satisfied. Responsibility depends on configuration and agreements.
A downloadable spreadsheet and low/moderate/high baselines are outside the clause-store task. SP 800-53B and its spreadsheets are separate sources.
Boundary and external-service responsibilities need RMF and service agreements. The catalog can supply related duties but not decide the actual boundary.
The question needs FedRAMP program requirements and parameter values beyond the NIST catalog.
The catalog supplies event-selection and generation duties. It does not specify Kiwi Syslog or OS rule settings. CUI alone does not determine the applicable framework.
The question names DISA/DAAPM and a classified-system context. Do not replace that authority with generic catalog clauses.

The source title explicitly requests Revision 5. The response clause has a selection with one or more choices and a separate alert duty. Read the parameter definitions as well as the statement. The scan-frequency clause c.1 is not part of this question.
Organization-defined conditions and inactivity periods do not establish that 364 days is acceptable. Federal legal deadlines and risk acceptance are outside this catalog.
The question seeks an authoritative cross-framework mapping. The clause store is not such a mapping.
The first clause concerns system flaws. Choosing operational resilience controls or a bug-tracking product depends on the failure and environment.
Catalog clauses do not provide a web-server control-family assignment template. Baselines, scoping and technology-specific implementation guidance are additional inputs.
Separate storage capacity from retention requirements. Record numeric values and justifications only from an actual organizational profile or external tailoring process.
An assessment plan and report are related catalog duties. A complete assessment method requires SP 800-53A and organizational/contractual scope.
The catalog explains organization-defined account types and session limits. Operational acceptability to admins and numeric limits require organization-specific decisions.
Policy, procedures and implementation are distinct. FedRAMP acceptance and the specific document format require additional authority.
Confirm the logout versus lock distinction. The catalog guidance itself refers to AC-11 for automatic logout even though AC-11 is device lock. Preserve that source inconsistency.
